title: Macro-banked Llama7B RMSNorm Phase-3 physical anchor
hypothesis: Replacing the failed full-row/full-gamma register arrays with exactly 64 characterized 64x32 proxy macros preserves exact Phase-3 behavior and yields a routable LANES=16 RMSNorm baseline whose latency, macro area, controller area, and power can be recosted honestly.

direct_comparison.primary_question: Does exact macro-banked Phase-3 RMSNorm become physically feasible, and does three-credit pipelining improve 1800-cycle conservative service to 1035 cycles without materially worsening PPA?
baselines: the merged two-row synthesis boundary from prop_l1_decoder_llama7b_rmsnorm_phase3_bounded_physical_v1
the 776-cycle but physically non-credible inferred-register Phase-3 schedule
include: exactly 64 fakeram45_64x32 macros organized as 16 lane banks by four depth shards
two-cycle registered macro reads with one outstanding request
three-credit pipelined reads bounded by the existing elastic arithmetic pipeline
full Phase-3 arithmetic, framing, exponent-255, row accounting, and backpressure equivalence
separate macro and standard-cell area plus routed timing and vectorless power
exclude: activity-backed power until a matched routed VCD follow-on

required_evaluations.objective: Compare the conservative and three-credit exact 64-macro LANES=16 Phase-3 RMSNorm controllers on Nangate45.

remaining_abstractions: FakeRAM is a characterized physical proxy rather than foundry SRAM signoff.
The conservative controller measures 1800 no-stall cycles and the three-credit candidate measures 1035; routed PPA must determine whether the extra control is Pareto-beneficial.
Power is vectorless until workload activity is replayed on the matching routed hierarchy.
